notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($197,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Colorado county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-14. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Colorado yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Real-time crime center
redFlags.detail: The Mesa County Sheriff's Office operates a real-time crime center.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS016137, citing KJCT-8

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Mesa County Sheriff’s Office received an enterprise license for LexisNexis' Accurint Virtual Crime Center through its membership in the Colorado Information Sharing Consortium.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012773, citing Government information

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Mesa County Sheriff's Office operates two Draganfly Innovations drones as of 2009, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003554, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College

redFlags.label: Private camera registry
redFlags.detail: The Mesa Countty Sheriff's Office maintains a community camera registry via CRIMEWATCH.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS016138, citing CRIMEWATCH
